items.front: In Route 53, the zone apex example.com must point to a load balancer. Which record do you create?
items.back: An alias record.
items.extra: Unlike a CNAME record, [you can create an alias record](../facts/route53.md#route53-alias-allowed-at-zone-apex) at the zone apex.

items.front: In Route 53, can you create a CNAME record at the zone apex, for example example.com?
items.back: No. The DNS protocol does not allow it.
items.extra: The [DNS protocol does not allow you to create](../facts/route53.md#route53-cname-dns-protocol-forbids-zone-apex) a CNAME record at the zone apex, so use an alias record there.

items.front: In Route 53, resources run in several Regions and each user must reach the Region with the best latency. Which routing policy do you choose?
items.back: Latency routing.
items.extra: Latency routing sends each user to [the Region that provides the best latency](../facts/route53.md#route53-choose-latency-routing-best-latency-region).

items.front: Route 53 health check or Elastic Load Balancing health check: which one changes the DNS answers for a record?
items.back: The Route 53 health check.
items.extra: If a Route 53 health check finds the resource unhealthy, [Route 53 routes traffic away from the associated record](../facts/route53.md#route53-dns-failover-routes-traffic-away-from-unhealthy-record).

items.front: In Route 53, every record in a group of records is unhealthy. Does Route 53 return no answer?
items.back: No. It treats all of them as healthy and answers.
items.extra: Route 53 [considers all the records in the group](../facts/route53.md#route53-no-record-healthy-all-records-considered-healthy) to be healthy and [selects one based on the routing policy](../facts/route53.md#route53-no-record-healthy-all-records-considered-healthy).

items.front: In Route 53 VPC Resolver, on-premises DNS servers must resolve names in a private hosted zone. What do you create?
items.back: An inbound Resolver endpoint.
items.extra: [Inbound Resolver endpoints allow DNS queries](../facts/route53.md#route53-resolver-inbound-endpoint-definition) to your VPC [from your on-premises network or another VPC](../facts/route53.md#route53-resolver-inbound-endpoint-definition).

items.front: In Route 53, compliance requires stable routing from each country to one chosen Region. Which routing policy do you choose?
items.back: Geolocation routing.
items.extra: Geolocation routing sends traffic [based on the location of your users](../facts/route53.md#route53-choose-geolocation-routing-user-location), not on measured latency.

items.front: In Route 53 geolocation routing without a default record, does a user from an unlisted country get an address?
items.back: No. Route 53 returns a no answer response.
items.extra: [If you don't create a default record](../facts/route53.md#route53-geolocation-no-default-no-answer), Route 53 [returns a "no answer" response](../facts/route53.md#route53-geolocation-no-default-no-answer) for those locations.

items.front: In Route 53, is multivalue answer routing a substitute for a load balancer?
items.back: No. AWS says it is not a load balancer substitute.
items.extra: Route 53 [returns only values for healthy resources](../facts/route53.md#route53-multivalue-purpose-not-lb-substitute), and AWS says [this isn't a substitute for a load balancer](../facts/route53.md#route53-multivalue-purpose-not-lb-substitute).

items.front: In Route 53, can a health check test an endpoint by its private IP address?
items.back: No. Health checkers cannot reach private IP ranges.
items.extra: [Route 53 cannot check the health of endpoints](../facts/route53.md#route53-hc-cannot-check-private-ip-ranges) with addresses in [local, private, nonroutable, or multicast ranges](../facts/route53.md#route53-hc-cannot-check-private-ip-ranges).

items.front: In Route 53, an instance in a VPC has only a private IP address. How do you check its health?
items.back: A health check that watches a CloudWatch alarm.
items.extra: Create a [CloudWatch metric, associate an alarm with the metric](../facts/route53.md#route53-hc-private-endpoint-cloudwatch-alarm-health-check), then a health check [based on the data stream for the alarm](../facts/route53.md#route53-hc-private-endpoint-cloudwatch-alarm-health-check).

items.front: In Route 53, a failover alias record points to a load balancer. How does the record follow the load balancer's health?
items.back: Set Evaluate Target Health to true on the alias record.
items.extra: For DNS failover to a load balancer, set the [“Evaluate Target Health” parameter to true](../facts/route53.md#route53-faq-elb-failover-alias-evaluate-target-health) instead of creating a separate health check.

items.front: In Route 53, you must change a critical record next week. What do you do first?
items.back: Temporarily shorten the TTL of the record.
items.extra: AWS recommends that you [temporarily shorten the TTLs](../facts/route53.md#route53-best-practice-shorten-ttl-before-critical-change), so that you can observe and roll back quickly.

items.front: In Route 53, can you set the TTL of an alias record that points to an AWS resource?
items.back: No. Route 53 uses the default TTL of the resource.
items.extra: For an alias record to an AWS resource, [you can't set the time to live (TTL)](../facts/route53.md#route53-alias-to-aws-resource-ttl-not-settable).

items.front: In Route 53 VPC Resolver, instances must resolve names that on-premises DNS servers host. What do you create?
items.back: An outbound Resolver endpoint with a forwarding rule.
items.extra: [Outbound Resolver endpoints allow DNS queries](../facts/route53.md#route53-resolver-outbound-endpoint-definition) [from your VPC to your on-premises network](../facts/route53.md#route53-resolver-outbound-endpoint-definition); rules decide [which DNS queries Resolver endpoint forwards to DNS resolvers](../facts/route53.md#route53-resolver-rules-control-forwarding).

items.front: In Route 53 VPC Resolver, can on-premises DNS servers forward queries to the VPC CIDR plus two address?
items.back: No. Use a Resolver inbound endpoint instead.
items.extra: Forwarding to a VPC CIDR plus two address [is not supported, and can cause unstable results](../facts/route53.md#route53-resolver-cidr-plus-two-forwarding-unsupported).

items.front: In Route 53, a private hosted zone matches the name but has no record for it. Does VPC Resolver then ask public DNS?
items.back: No. It returns NXDOMAIN to the client.
items.extra: VPC Resolver [doesn't forward the request to a public DNS](../facts/route53.md#route53-matching-phz-no-record-returns-nxdomain) resolver in this case.

items.front: In Route 53, a small share of users must test a new version of the software. Which routing policy do you choose?
items.back: Weighted routing.
items.extra: Weighted routing sends traffic to [multiple resources in proportions that you specify](../facts/route53.md#route53-choose-weighted-routing-proportions).

items.front: In Route 53, can you use IP-based routing for records in a private hosted zone?
items.back: No.
items.extra: [You cannot use IP-based routing policy](../facts/route53.md#route53-ip-based-routing-not-in-private-hosted-zone) for records in a private hosted zone.

items.front: In Route 53, failover between Regions must work while the control plane is impaired. What do you rely on?
items.back: Health check status, not changes to records.
items.extra: AWS says [you should not rely on the Route 53 control plane in your recovery path](../facts/route53.md#route53-fi-no-control-plane-in-recovery-path); use the [status of health checks to perform failovers](../facts/route53.md#route53-fi-no-control-plane-in-recovery-path).

items.front: In Route 53, the domain registration stays with another registrar. What must that registrar change?
items.back: The name servers of the domain, to those of the hosted zone.
items.extra: Tell the registrar to [update the name servers for your domain](../facts/route53.md#route53-faq-external-registrar-must-update-name-servers) to the ones of your hosted zone.

items.front: In Amazon S3 with Route 53, can a bucket website endpoint serve your domain with HTTPS?
items.back: No. Put a CloudFront distribution in front of the bucket.
items.extra: A website endpoint [doesn't support SSL/TLS](../facts/route53.md#route53-s3-website-endpoint-no-https), so [use the S3 bucket as the origin for the distribution](../facts/route53.md#route53-s3-website-endpoint-no-https).

items.front: In Route 53, geolocation routing or geoproximity routing: which one uses a bias to shift traffic?
items.back: Geoproximity routing.
items.extra: [A bias expands or shrinks the geographic region](../facts/route53.md#route53-geoproximity-bias-expands-or-shrinks-region) from which traffic goes to a resource.

items.front: In a VPC, a compromised instance could send data out through DNS lookups. Which Route 53 feature blocks those queries?
items.back: DNS Firewall in Route 53 VPC Resolver.
items.extra: A primary use of DNS Firewall is to [help prevent DNS exfiltration of your data](../facts/route53.md#route53-dns-firewall-blocks-dns-exfiltration); [DNS Firewall is a feature of Route 53 VPC Resolver](../facts/route53.md#route53-dnsfw-feature-of-vpc-resolver-no-extra-setup).

items.front: In Route 53, each new hosted zone gets {{c1::a unique set of four name servers}} by default.
In Route 53, AWS recommends a TTL of {{c1::60 seconds or less}} for a record with a health check.
In Route 53, the default request interval of a health check is {{c1::30 seconds}}.
In Route 53, the default failure threshold of a health check is {{c1::three health checks}}.
In Route 53, an endpoint is healthy if {{c1::more than 18%}} of the health checkers report it healthy.
In Route 53, multivalue answer routing answers each DNS query with {{c1::up to eight healthy records}}.
In Route 53, the weight of a weighted record is an integer {{c1::between 0 and 255}}.
In Route 53, record changes generally reach all Route 53 servers {{c1::within 60 seconds}}.
In Route 53, a name must return the IPv6 address of a web server. Which record type do you create?
items.back: An AAAA record.
items.extra: An AAAA record routes traffic [using an IPv6 address](../facts/route53.md#route53-aaaa-record-ipv6); an A record uses an IPv4 address.
